issues.text: In short: GAM says a bigger fuel credit "would put upward pressure on base rates," ... issues.text: Evidence (line 226): Mixed (whether where the money is credited changes what each customer group pays: GIPL says it does, and that Georgia Power disagrees) / Who disagrees: By GIPL's account, Georgia Power holds that where the money is credited does not change what each group pays. {analysis: P-102}
issues.problem: Every other 'Mixed' grade cites the disputing party's own words. This one rests only on GIPL's description of Georgia Power's view. The record that is public supports the factual premise: GAM's cost-study table (P-116) shows customer groups pay different shares of fuel and base costs, and the page's own analysis (line 106) relies on that. Under the page's rubric ('parties give conflicting accounts'), a second-hand account is not a conflicting account. Card 5 ends up the only card with no 'Supported' element, and that comes from how the rubric was applied, not from the evidence.
issues.fix: Either cite Georgia Power's own words in 'Who disagrees' and the label (P-124: base-side real-time money "is reducing other costs recovered through base rates"), or grade the premise 'Supported (no party whose testimony we could read disputes that customer groups pay different shares of fuel and base costs [P-116, P-102]); GIPL says Georgia Power disagrees that this matters here.'

verdict_summary: The page passes the hard rules. It uses one template for every card and plan, prints its evidence rubric, and treats redactions as unknown, not zero. There are no loaded words outside quotes, and says/said use is even across parties. There are no party labels, no minors or private addresses, no anticipated arguments and no ratings. 'What you can do' is neutral, and values disputes are framed as legitimate. The remaining neutrality problems are about placement and space, not slanted wording. Card 9's 'In short' gives GAM's opponents most of its 67 words. Card 5's 'Mixed' grade rests on GIPL's account of Georgia Power. The page's own voice answers challenges for GIPL and GAM only. Plan C drops the 'base rates could rise later' sentence that Plans B and D carry. Cards 1 and 5 leave out the reasons that the other cards give. A few claims go past their sources: the $1.35 look-back reads as a promise, 'every proposed change' is too broad, and 'homes come out behind only if nearly all of it does' hides its assumptions. Clarity is the weaker side. The 30-second item 2 (92 words) and the decision block (about 117 words against about 80) are over budget. Labels run 61-86 words, and the base-side block and the cards read at about grade 9-14, with undefined terms. Fix the medium items before publishing; the low ones can wait for the next revision.
